title: Protesters march in Dublin against gender-based violence

tea.why: Protesters gathered to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women and demand action against gender-based violence.
tea.want: The group demanded stronger action against perpetrators of gender-based violence and increased support for survivors.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Hundreds of people marched from Barnardo Square to the Department of Justice in Dublin city centre.

summary: On November 25, 2026, hundreds of people gathered in Dublin for the 'Rise Up! Justice for Survivors' demonstration to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. Organised by Rosa Soc Fem, the march began at Barnardo Square and proceeded to the Department of Justice. Participants highlighted issues including sexual violence, rape culture, and victim-blaming. The protest also expressed solidarity with survivors and referenced the #IamJaneDoe campaign. Organisers described the event as anti-racist, anti-fascist, pro-trans, and pro-Palestine. During the march, participants chanted slogans against gender-based violence and named several public figures while calling for accountability. The demonstration followed the release of 2026 research from the Dublin Rape Crisis Centre regarding public attitudes toward sexual violence.
response: No official response reported in the sources.
